styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Batu Caves, the old mosque and colonial Merdeka Square.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Hawker stalls, mamak suppers and Chinatown classics.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Forest walks, the Lake Gardens and cool hill air.

stays.why: Walk to the Petronas Towers and the park. Best metro links and easy airport train from KL Sentral.
Malls, street food and nightlife on your doorstep. Central for walking to many sights.
Cheapest base for food and markets. Close to Merdeka Square and the old town.
Little India near KL Sentral, so airport trains and metro are minutes away. Good value.

food: Eat at hawker centres: Jalan Alor for grilled skewers and seafood, and Lot 10 Hutong for classic stalls in air-conditioning.
Try nasi lemak, char kway teow, laksa and roti canai. A hawker meal is often around RM 8–20.
Mamak restaurants (Indian-Muslim) are open late and cheap. Good for supper after a night out.
Chinatown and Petaling Street for noodles, dumplings and fresh juice; check prices before ordering seafood.
Alcohol is pricey and limited outside bars and hotels. Many places are halal; look for the sign.
more_time: Swap a city day for the Batu Caves in the morning, then the Forest Research Institute trails in the afternoon.
Take a day trip to Melaka or the Genting Highlands; buses and trains run from KL Sentral — check times on the day.
Add a night in the Cameron Highlands for cool air and tea plantations if you want a break from the heat.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the towers, the old town, Batu Caves and a hawker-food crawl, with time for rain delays.

month_notes: January: hot and wet, about 22 rain days. Plan indoor sights and carry a small umbrella.
February: the driest month, around 17 rain days. Best window for outdoor sights.
March: hotter and wetter again, about 25 rain days. Go out early and rest at midday.
April: one of the wettest months, about 28 rain days. Expect heavy afternoon storms.
May: still very wet, about 28 rain days. Keep plans flexible and indoor backups ready.
June: rain eases to about 23 days. Good for sightseeing between showers.
July: similar to June, about 22 rain days. Warm days around 31°C.
August: rain picks up, about 25 days. Short, heavy downpours are common.
September: about 25 rain days. Same pattern: hot, humid, stormy afternoons.
October: about 24 rain days. Still hot; watch the sky after lunch.
November: the wettest month, about 29 rain days. Pack rain gear and plan indoor days.
December: very wet, about 27 rain days. Expect showers most days; book flexible plans.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical and hot all year: highs around 30–32°C, lows around 23–24°C, and rain on most months. It is wettest from March to May and October to December.

items.title: Hot every month
items.text: Highs stay around 30–32°C and lows around 23–24°C all year. There is no cool season.

items.title: Rain is normal
items.text: Expect 17–29 rain days a month. February is driest; November is wettest.

items.title: Afternoon storms
items.text: Downpours are often short and heavy, usually later in the day. Plan outdoor sights for the morning.

items.title: High humidity
items.text: It feels muggy most days. Take breaks in air-conditioned malls and cafés.

items.title: Pack rain gear
items.text: A small umbrella or light rain jacket helps. Pavements can flood briefly after storms.

items.title: What to wear
items.text: Light, breathable clothes and comfortable shoes. A light layer for strong indoor AC. Cover shoulders and knees at mosques and temples.

transit.best: Use the RapidKL metro for most sights; Grab for late nights and places off the rail grid.

modes.text: RapidKL lines 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11 and 12 cover most sights. Trains every 2–7 minutes. Buy a Touch 'n Go card (RM10 plus top-up).
KTM lines 1, 2 and 10 and ERL lines 6 and 7 link KL Sentral to suburbs and the airport. Contactless cards work on KTM and ERL only.
Cheap but slow. Use buses for short hops off the rail grid.
Grab is the main ride app. Metered taxis exist but agree the fare first.
Driving is stressful in jams. Only worth it for trips out of the city.
Fine in the centre, but pavements are patchy. Watch your step and cross with care.
